questions.q: The rate law for a pure SN1 reaction of an alkyl halide RX is:
questions.e: The slow ionization of RX is unimolecular and independent of nucleophile concentration.

questions.q: Which carbocation is most stable?
questions.e: More alkyl substituents stabilize the cation by hyperconjugation and induction.

questions.q: Solvolysis of an enantiomerically pure tertiary alkyl halide by SN1 typically gives:
questions.e: The planar carbocation can be attacked from either face; some inversion excess from ion pairing is common.

questions.q: Which is the best leaving group?
questions.e: Good leaving groups are weak bases (conjugates of strong acids); tosylate is the conjugate base of TsOH (pKa ≈ −2.8).

questions.q: With a small strong base (e.g., NaOEt), E2 elimination of 2-bromobutane gives mainly:
questions.e: Zaitsev: the more substituted alkene predominates with unhindered bases.

questions.q: In E2 elimination of a substituted chlorocyclohexane in a chair conformation, the leaving group must be:
c: Axial, with an axial anti β-hydrogen
questions.e: Anti-periplanar geometry requires trans-diaxial arrangement in a chair.

questions.q: Compare E1 and E2 mechanisms in terms of rate law, base requirement and rearrangements.
questions.m: E2: single concerted step, rate = k[RX][base], requires a strong base, needs anti-periplanar H and LG, no carbocation so no rearrangements. E1: two steps via a carbocation, rate = k[RX], favored by weak bases/ionizing solvents and 3° substrates, can undergo carbocation rearrangements, and competes with SN1.

questions.q: Which reagents generate the electrophile NO₂⁺ for nitration of benzene?
questions.e: Sulfuric acid protonates nitric acid, which loses water to give the nitronium ion.

questions.q: The –OCH₃ group on a benzene ring is:
questions.e: Oxygen's lone pair donates by resonance, stabilizing o/p sigma complexes.

questions.q: The –NO₂ group on a benzene ring is:
questions.e: Strong electron withdrawal destabilizes the cationic sigma complex, least at the meta position.

questions.q: Friedel–Crafts acylation is often preferred over alkylation because:
c: The acylium ion does not rearrange and the ketone product is deactivated to further reaction
It uses a weaker Lewis acid
questions.e: Alkylation suffers from carbocation rearrangement and polyalkylation (alkylbenzene is more reactive).

questions.q: Outline how to make p-bromonitrobenzene versus m-bromonitrobenzene from benzene.
questions.m: Para: brominate first (Br₂/FeBr₃; Br is an o/p director), then nitrate (HNO₃/H₂SO₄) and separate the para from the ortho isomer. Meta: nitrate first (NO₂ is a meta director), then brominate with Br₂/FeBr₃ to give the meta isomer. Order of introducing substituents determines the pattern.

questions.q: An aldol addition requires that at least one carbonyl component possesses:
questions.e: An α-hydrogen is needed to form the enolate nucleophile.

questions.q: Treating 2-methylcyclohexanone with LDA at −78 °C gives mainly the:
questions.e: A bulky, strong base removes the less hindered α-proton irreversibly under kinetic control.

questions.q: The Claisen condensation of ethyl acetate with NaOEt gives:
questions.e: Enolate attacks a second ester, loses ethoxide; the product β-keto ester is deprotonated, driving the reaction.

questions.q: Show how the acetoacetic ester synthesis converts ethyl acetoacetate and ethyl bromide into 2-pentanone.
questions.m: Deprotonate ethyl acetoacetate at the doubly activated α-carbon (NaOEt), alkylate with CH₃CH₂Br (SN2) to give ethyl 2-ethylacetoacetate, then hydrolyze the ester (aq. acid or base then acid) and heat to decarboxylate the β-keto acid, giving CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ (2-pentanone).

questions.q: The Diels–Alder reaction forms:
c: A cyclohexene ring from a diene and a dienophile

questions.q: For a diene to undergo Diels–Alder it must be able to adopt the:
questions.e: Both termini must be able to reach the dienophile on the same face.

questions.q: In the reaction of cyclopentadiene with maleic anhydride, the kinetic product is the:
questions.e: Secondary orbital interactions stabilize the endo transition state.

questions.q: A Robinson annulation consists of:
c: A Michael addition followed by an intramolecular aldol condensation
questions.e: It builds a new six-membered cyclohexenone ring.

questions.q: Oxidation of a primary alcohol with PCC in CH₂Cl₂ gives:
questions.e: Anhydrous chromium(VI) conditions stop at the aldehyde; aqueous Jones conditions go to the acid.

questions.q: LiAlH₄ reduces a carboxylic acid (after workup) to:
questions.e: LiAlH₄ is a powerful hydride donor and reduces acids and esters to alcohols; NaBH₄ does not.
